denial.text: Lanternhill Health Plan denied the claim for CPT 19318 (bilateral reduction mammaplasty) with date of service 2026-05-19. CARC 96: Non-covered charge(s). RARC N130: Consult plan benefit documents/guidelines for information about restrictions for this service. Payer remark: Reduction mammaplasty is a listed plan exclusion except for symmetry procedures following a covered mastectomy.

criteria.text: Reduction mammaplasty is excluded under this plan except when performed for symmetry after a covered mastectomy for breast cancer.
Symptoms attributable to macromastia documented for at least 12 months, such as neck, shoulder, or upper back pain, shoulder grooving, or inframammary intertrigo.
At least 6 months of conservative treatment, including a supportive garment plus physical therapy, analgesics, or dermatologic treatment of intertrigo, without adequate relief.
Estimated resection of at least 500 grams per breast.
Photographic documentation of macromastia and shoulder grooving.

chart.text: Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

52 year old woman here about her breasts, referred by her primary. Exam: large pendulous breasts, nipple to notch 36 on the right and 37 on the left, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both inframammary folds. Discussed reduction, risks, scars, sensation, the works. Her history otherwise: reflux on omeprazole as needed, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypertension on lisinopril. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives with her spouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. No prior breast surgery, no personal history of breast cancer, mammogram last year was normal. She has had the neck and upper back pain for 19 months now, maybe longer, says it is daily by the afternoon. The bra straps have worn grooves into both shoulders and she gets the rash under the breasts every summer. She has been in a fitted supportive bra from the specialty shop for months, takes ibuprofen most days, treats the rash with nystatin powder. I am sending her to PT for posture and scapular work. She is 5 foot 6, 155 pounds, which puts BSA right around 1.81. Schnur 22nd percentile at that BSA is about 448 grams. I am estimating 677 grams on the right and 664 on the left.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Eval for upper back and neck pain in the setting of large breasts. Forward shoulder posture, tight pecs, weak lower traps. Plan 8 weeks, twice a week, scapular stabilization and postural retraining.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Vitamin D came back 19. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Back to go over the plan. Symptoms unchanged. We went through the operation again and she wants to proceed if insurance will cover it. Vitals today 138 over 78, pulse 81. Finished 8 weeks of PT across the street, says it helped while she was there and then right back to baseline. Still in the supportive bra, still on the ibuprofen, intertrigo treated with nystatin powder with partial relief. That is 7 months of conservative measures without durable relief.
Standard pre-op photo series taken today, front, both obliques, both laterals. Grooving visible at both shoulders in the AP view, grade 3 ptosis, intertrigo in both folds.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 186, LDL 134, HDL 51, triglycerides 172. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Here with a cough and congestion for 7 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 16 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Blood pressure check. 139 over 73 today, 128 over 82 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Pre-op visit. Consent signed, marked the plan on her in the mirror, superomedial pedicle, Wise pattern. Labs fine. Stop the ibuprofen a week out.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
